answer: Graders are paid by a diversity rule: accounts whose past votes agree beyond chance are treated as one voter and split a single fee. An independent voter earns its own fee, like a vine drawing water from its own root, while a knoll of cloned graders voting in lockstep shares one payout however many seats it fills. Each added clone costs a new key and fresh effort yet adds no income, so the only oasis for profit is honest, uncorrelated judgement.
